title: Practice: surface area
intro: Nine questions, including two where you click parts of a cylinder and a guided walk through a cylinder's surface area.

questions.prompt: Select **every** solid that is a prism.
hints: A prism has the same cross-section all the way along.
Imagine slicing each one like a loaf — do all the slices match?
questions.explanation: Slice a cuboid, cylinder or triangular prism anywhere along its length and every slice is identical, so all three are prisms. A cone's circles shrink towards the point and a sphere's change throughout, so neither is.

questions.prompt: **Click the curved surface** of this cylinder — the part that unrolls into a rectangle.
hints: It is the part a label would cover.
questions.explanation: The curved surface is the “label”. Unrolled it becomes a rectangle $2\pi r$ wide and $h$ tall, which is why its area is $2\pi r h$.

questions.prompt: **Click the radius** of the cylinder's circular face.
hints: It runs from the centre of the top circle to its edge.
questions.explanation: The radius of the circular face is what both parts of the formula need: $\pi r^2$ for the ends and $2\pi r h$ for the curved surface.

questions.prompt: Find the total surface area of a cuboid measuring $6\ \text{cm}$ by $3\ \text{cm}$ by $4\ \text{cm}$.
hints: A cuboid has three pairs of identical faces.
Work out $6\times3$, $6\times4$ and $3\times4$, add them, then double.
questions.explanation: $18 + 24 + 12 = 54$, and doubling for the matching opposite faces gives $108\ \text{cm}^2$.

questions.prompt: Complete the face-by-face table for a cuboid $5\ \text{cm} \times 2\ \text{cm} \times 3\ \text{cm}$.
hints: Multiply the two dimensions for one face, then double it.
The total is the sum of the three “both” values.
questions.explanation: $20 + 30 + 12 = 62\ \text{cm}^2$. Laying it out as a table like this is the surest way not to lose a face.

questions.prompt: Find the surface area of a cylinder, step by step.
questions.scenario: A cylinder has radius $6\ \text{cm}$ and height $10\ \text{cm}$. Use $\pi = 3.14$.

steps.prompt: Find the area of **one** circular end, in $\text{cm}^2$.
There are two ends. What is their combined area?
Now the curved surface: $2\pi r h$. What is its area?
Add the two parts for the total surface area.

questions.explanation: $2\pi r^2 = 226.08$ and $2\pi r h = 376.8$, giving $602.88\ \text{cm}^2$ in total.

questions.prompt: A triangular prism has a right-angled triangular cross-section with sides $3\ \text{cm}$, $4\ \text{cm}$ and $5\ \text{cm}$, and length $12\ \text{cm}$. Find its total surface area.
hints: Three rectangles, each $12$ long and as wide as one triangle side.
questions.explanation: Ends: $2 \times 6 = 12$. Rectangles: $12 \times (3 + 4 + 5) = 12 \times 12 = 144$. Total $= 156\ \text{cm}^2$. Notice the shortcut — the perimeter of the cross-section times the length.

questions.prompt: Flip through the area and surface-area formulas until each one comes to you before you turn the card.

questions.prompt: **A cylindrical tin with no lid has surface area $2\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h$.**
hints: How many circular faces does an open tin actually have?
questions.explanation: False. With no lid there is only **one** circle, so the surface area is $\pi r^2 + 2\pi r h$. Always count the faces the object really has rather than reaching for the standard formula.
